turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve been very irritable and my mood has been unstable recently. I also have sharp, sensitive pain with an intensity of 8/10, mainly in both ears (right and left), with about 8/10 location precision and a pace of 5/10.

[REASONING]
Key findings so far: mood instability/irritability; sharp, very sensitive bilateral ear pain (8/10) with high location precision (8/10) and moderate pace (5/10). No other symptoms provided yet (fever, sore throat, cough, breathing issues, neurologic symptoms, discharge, hearing loss, trauma).
Top candidates (tentative):
1) Acute otitis media — ear pain can be severe; often unilateral but can be bilateral, especially with viral illness; would be supported by fever, recent URI, ear fullness, decreased hearing, or tympanic membrane findings.
2) Acute laryngitis / viral pharyngitis / URTI — can cause referred ear pain via Eustachian tube dysfunction; would be supported by sore throat, cough, nasal symptoms.
3) Acute dystonic reactions — can cause painful sensations and agitation/irritability, but “ear pain” specifically is less typical; would be supported by sudden abnormal neck/jaw movements or muscle spasms.
4) Panic attack — can cause irritability/anxiety and “sharp” discomfort, but true ear pain is less typical; would be supported by episodes with palpitations, dyspnea, fear, tingling.
5) Anemia — can cause irritability but not focal sharp ear pain; unlikely without fatigue/pallor.
